references.text: The disciples came to Jesus and asked him why he spoke to the people in parables. Jesus explained that it had been given to them to know the secrets of the kingdom of heaven, but not to others. This parallel shows the same situation where the disciples ask about the meaning of a parable.

Mark's parallel account describes those who were around Jesus with the twelve asking him about the parables. Jesus explained the difference between those given insight into the secret of God's kingdom and those who were outside.

The immediately following verse where Jesus answers the disciples' question and explains that it has been given to them to know the secrets of God's kingdom, while others receive these things in parables.
The disciples ask Jesus to explain the parable of the weeds in the field, showing the repeated pattern where the disciples seek a private explanation for Jesus' parables.
Mark reports that Jesus spoke the word to the people in parables, but explained everything privately to his disciples. This sheds light on the context of the disciples' question in Luke 8:9.
Peter asks Jesus to explain the parable to them, showing the same pattern where the disciples seek an explanation for Jesus' figurative speech.
